Stat leaders

Who gets the most of the points that don't come from goals and assists. Pick a stat, then narrow it to a position or to players available in Hope Bros. Bonus goes to the three best players in each match by FPL's BPS score (3, 2, 1). Clean sheets are worth 4 to keepers and defenders and 1 to midfielders, for 60+ minutes without conceding. Defensive contribution (DC) is 2 points for 10+ clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles (defenders), or 12+ of those plus recoveries (midfielders and forwards). Each box is one game: the gameweek, the points, the opponent (H or A).

Each game shows the bookmakers' chances of a home win, draw or away win, the favourite, and the predicted score (the likeliest score for the favourite result, so draws show when a draw is most likely), plus the three likeliest exact scorelines, worked out from the match result and over/under 2.5 goals odds averaged across firms. Clean sheet chances use the same numbers. 1 of 10 games are flagged: Goals likely = strong attack vs leaky defense, Clean sheet spot = tight defense vs weak attack. Games are in kickoff order (Eastern time).

Compare players

Line up to 4 players side by side. Search any player, filter by club, position or who owns him, tap + Compare anywhere in the report, or pick one of yours and tap Find replacements for the full list at his position. Green = best in that row. Your tests row: above the bar means his points a week over his team's last 3 gameweeks beat what a counted player at his position scores for the rest of Hope Bros (GK 4.4 · DEF 4.1 · MID 3.8 · FWD 4.0); nailed means he started the last 3 and averaged 80+ minutes.

Team builder

Build any 15: 2 keepers, 5 defenders, 5 midfielders and 3 forwards, with 11 starting. Start from your own squad or from scratch, then tap an empty spot to add a player, tap a player to see why he's predicted what he is, and tap a starter and then a sub to swap them. The team is saved in this browser. Predicted points are an estimate built from parts: minutes, goals and assists from his xG and xA against how leaky the opponent is, clean-sheet chances from both teams' numbers, his DC and bonus rates, and his cards. Checked against GW7-9, the predictions averaged within 0.1 of what players actually scored.

Watch list

Players you like, with your reason, tracked from the gameweek after you add them, whether you sign them or not. Each pick gets a verdict once it has 2 gameweeks: Good call if he's averaged at least a point a week above the bar for his position, Miss if a point below, otherwise About average. Picks are saved on GitHub, so they last all season and show on any device.

Add a player

Opens GitHub with everything filled in; tap Create there. It shows up here in about two minutes.

Your moves this season

Every waiver claim and free-agent pickup you've made. Each move gets two ratings. Pickup: did the player you brought in beat the bar for his position while he was yours, and outscore the player you dropped over the same gameweeks? Drop: did the player you let go fall below the bar afterwards, and get outscored by his replacement? Good = both, Bad = neither, Mixed = one of the two. Players you moved more than once are rated for each move.

What the top 1,000 own

Squads of the 1,000 highest-ranked managers in the main FPL game, checked once per gameweek after the deadline. Top 1,000 is the share of them who own the player; change is how that moved since the previous gameweek for the same managers, which is where you spot them piling in. Everyone is ownership across all FPL managers, and edge is the gap: players the best managers rate well ahead of the crowd. These are budget-game squads (a £100m budget, and anyone can own anyone), so treat it as a read on who they rate, not a Draft ranking. Managers using a Free Hit that week are left out.

Prediction tracker

A season-long experiment: a predicted result, score, clean sheets and goalscorers for every match, saved before kickoff and graded after full time. Predictions refresh with the latest team news until each match kicks off, then they're locked. Predictions use betting odds where available, with the stats model logged alongside for comparison.
